solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Baffles are wooden posts

definitions.meaning: to baffle someone is to stump them, so baffles is the verb sense
the three upright sticks of a cricket wicket

explanation.surface: Some puzzling structures turn out to be nothing but timber posts.
explanation.walkthrough: STUMPS are the three wooden uprights of a cricket wicket; as a verb, 'stumps' means puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump someone is to leave them puzzled; cricket stumps are wooden uprights.

clue.text: Revenue obtained from executing wishes

indicators.note: executing someone is beheading them, so the first letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: yearnings are longings or wishes

explanation.surface: Income gained from carrying out people's wishes, like a genie for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executing' cuts the head, Y, from YEARNINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money taken in, a synonym for revenue.

clue.text: Times includes rating model family employee

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: by as in multiplication, three by four
an able seaman, a naval rating, is abbreviated AB
a sitter is someone who models for an artist

explanation.surface: A newspaper's ratings model applied to a household worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper: it is BY, as in multiplying three by four. A naval rating, an able seaman, is AB.
explanation.definitionFit: A babysitter is paid by a family to mind its children.

clue.text: One accommodated in flat getting compensated

indicators.note: being housed in a place means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: pad is slang for a flat or home
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A lodger housed in an apartment gets paid back.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid means compensated, given money for work or loss.

clue.text: Turnout after nine, before the ball

indicators.note: the time phrase comes in front of the next piece

parts.note: the hour after nine o'clock is at ten
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: The crowd that arrives late in the evening, ahead of the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnout is the number of people attending, another word for attendance.

clue.text: How to wear one's hair for a change

indicators.note: changing the letters of the two short words rearranges them

explanation.surface: A suggestion for a new hairstyle, just to be different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges FORA (from 'for a').
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle, one way of wearing hair.

clue.text: Manage to support most of finance for such an event

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece underneath holds up the one above
all but the last letter of the synonym is kept

parts.note: to fund is to finance
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Organisers find most of the money to back a charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops D from FUND; in a down entry RUN 'supports' FUN by sitting beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fun run is a charity running event, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Sort of injury sustained by a couple of cats?

parts.note: a cat, as in cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
the cat, a flogging scourge, is also a lash

explanation.surface: An injury suffered from an encounter with two felines.
explanation.walkthrough: The cats are not animals: 'cat' is short for cat-o'-nine-tails, so two of them give two words for a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiplash is a neck injury from sudden jerking, as in a car crash.

clue.text: Criticise a character chasing rent

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so these pieces come after

parts.note: a rent is a tear in cloth
a part is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: A tenant character pursuing someone over unpaid rent.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear apart is to criticise savagely.

clue.text: Fine heavy drinker with a load of cash

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a lush is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A well-off drunk with plenty of money to spend on drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush is slang for having plenty of money.

clue.text: 10's half a day with viewers

indicators.note: only half the letters of the weekday are kept

parts.note: Monday is a day of the week
viewers are eyes, so having them is eyed

explanation.surface: Someone spends half a day in front of an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 refers to the answer at 10-across, FLUSH; the 's means 'is'. 'half' keeps MON from MONDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed and the earlier answer both mean rich, having plenty of cash.

clue.text: Journey in which content of language got riper

indicators.note: the contents of the phrase are what it holds inside it

explanation.surface: A linguist notes that the words grew riper on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' takes the letters inside 'language got riper'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is self-indulgent behaviour, here treated literally as a journey.

clue.text: Notice abandoning good for evil

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a sign is a posted notice

explanation.surface: A notice turning its back on good in favour of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops G from SIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sin is moral wrongdoing, a synonym for evil.

clue.text: Obstruction confronting source of American army's baggage

indicators.note: confronting means standing in front of, so this piece comes first

parts.note: an impediment is an obstacle

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A roadblock faces American troops and their equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Impedimenta is a Latin word for baggage and supplies carried by an army.

clue.text: They make suits fit if plans go astray

indicators.note: plans going wrong means the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A tailor's plans go wrong, and the suits still fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go astray' rearranges FITIFPLANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaintiffs are people who bring lawsuits.

clue.text: Royal contact's ability to make 19?

parts.note: the legendary king whose touch turned everything to gold, read here as a knack for making money

explanation.surface: A monarch's handshake that can make cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 refers to 19-across, meaning money. King Midas's touch turned everything to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midas touch is the knack of making money from every venture.

clue.text: Mail accepts one as a given proposition

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: post is mail
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: The postal service takes in something as a matter of fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts I inside POST.
explanation.definitionFit: A posit is a statement assumed true as the basis of argument.

clue.text: Cycle set in cycle stand

indicators.note: the cycled word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: to pedal is to cycle

indicators.note: cycling the word's letters round shifts them into a new order

explanation.surface: A bicycle is set up in a bike rack.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Cycle' is the instruction, cycling the letters of 'set' round; the second is the verb meaning to pedal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is a base or stand on which a statue rests.

clue.text: New name given to a girl

indicators.note: these letters are attached to the end of the short word

explanation.surface: A newborn girl is given a new name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a common female name, so a girl.

clue.text: What one might need, say, is cash

definitions.meaning: said aloud, need sounds like knead, and bread mix is what one kneads

explanation.surface: Asking what one requires, and the answer is money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that 'need' stands for its sound-alike 'knead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakers knead bread mix, and the same word is slang for money.

clue.text: Speed reduced — that's a blow!

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine, an upper
something cut has been reduced

explanation.surface: A speed limit lowered, and drivers find it a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is an upward punch, a blow in boxing.

clue.text: Late sign of hesitation during calls for doubles

parts.note: the late person is dead

indicators.note: one piece occurs within the other

parts.note: rings are phone calls
er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A late hesitation in phone calls, from people who sound the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' in crosswords often means dead, as in 'the late king'; 'calls' are telephone rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead ringers are people who look exactly alike, doubles.

clue.text: Ships that supply weapons to an American lawyer

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons
an is the indefinite article, A
a DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: Vessels that deliver weapons to a lawyer in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'that' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, a large group of ships.

clue.text: Lay bet with no name

indicators.note: having none of means the letter is taken out

parts.note: a punt is a bet

explanation.surface: An anonymous gambler places a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops N from PUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something down is to put it there.

clue.text: Score century finally, after time passed

indicators.note: the piece before comes after these, so they lead

parts.note: went means passed, as time goes by

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A cricketer reaches a century just as time runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, as in threescore years and ten.

clue.text: Pure heart possessed by beaten Masai warrior

indicators.note: being possessed means being held inside the other piece
beaten suggests knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A Masai warrior with a pure heart, beaten in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' rearranges MASAI to SAMAI, and the Masai are themselves a warrior people, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of the Japanese warrior class.

clue.text: Step on it — it's just grass!

definitions.meaning: hurry up, a command to go faster
a marsh plant with hollow stems, used for matting

explanation.surface: Told to hurry, but it's only a lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush is to hurry; rushes are grass-like waterside plants.

clue.text: Start to show bravery dropping a whip

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
dropping means losing, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: courage is bravery

explanation.surface: Showing courage and letting go of a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes A out of COURAGE to give COURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip used for punishment.

clue.text: Teacher with key for old address

parts.note: pupils call a male teacher sir
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A teacher with a key to an old building.
explanation.definitionFit: Sire was an old form of address to a king or lord.

clue.text: Mountains in the Libyan desert

indicators.note: the answer lies within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Peaks found out in the Saharan sands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes the run spanning 'Libyan desert'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the mountain range of South America.

clue.text: Where cars may be sold by tribunal after warning

indicators.note: this piece comes after the warning in the answer

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout
a court is a tribunal

explanation.surface: A judgment handed down after a warning, in a car dealer's lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecourt is the area in front of a garage or showroom where cars are displayed.
